prompt: According to the lesson, where does governance start?

choices.text: With a policy signed by the board
choices.why: The policy comes later in the lesson.

choices.text: With a certification audit
choices.why: Certification is the last thing, not the first.

choices.text: With knowing which systems exist
choices.why: Right: nothing protects a system nobody knows is running.

choices.text: With a security review of every change
choices.why: A review needs a system to review.

prompt: Why must one approver be somebody who is not the author?

choices.text: Authors are not allowed to read their own changes before merging
choices.why: They read them; it is not enough.

choices.text: The owner is always the author
choices.why: Here the owner is Ana and the author Bruno.

choices.text: Two names make the review faster
choices.why: They make it slower, on purpose.

choices.text: An author checks what they meant, not what they wrote
choices.why: Right.

prompt: Why is each approval beside evidence rather than a signature on the whole change?
hint: Somebody reads it a year later.

choices.text: Signatures cannot be stored in JSON
choices.why: They can; the point is what they say.

choices.text: It shows later readers what was checked
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Evidence replaces the need for approvals
choices.why: Both are needed.

choices.text: The suite reads the signatures
choices.why: The suite runs checks; it reads no signatures.

prompt: Why does the last line of the policy, that whoever finds a problem may stop the system, need a policy rather than a program?

choices.why: They can; the question is who may.

choices.text: Without it, people wait for permission
choices.why: Right: and lesson 24 showed what waiting costs.

choices.text: The ANPD requires it in writing
choices.why: The course does not say so.

choices.text: It only applies outside working hours
choices.why: It applies whenever a problem is found.
